info.description:
Go + PocketBase backend for QuantumAtlas: paper
collection + search + database. Write endpoints and
the search/paper read surface require a bearer token
(PAT or PocketBase session) plus the matching scope.
See the auth model docs for the scope vocabulary.
info.title: QuantumAtlas API

get.description: Admin-only: find papers with at least one asset.

Admin-only asset listing: every PDF / markdown object the
paper owns, with S3 object keys, sizes, SHA256s.
Admin-only proxy stream with Content-Disposition: attachment.
Admin-only: time-limited presigned URL for direct browser-to-S3.

Read-only introspection of the QATLAS_POSTGRES_DSN database:
every table in schema public (goose_db_version included,
alphabetical) with row estimate, total size, columns
(type/nullable/default/is_pk), indexes and constraints.
Admin-only: session token + is_admin or is_superadmin
on the users record.

200.description: {database, tables:[{name, row_estimate, total_size, columns, indexes, constraints}]}

post.description:
Returns {url} — a short-lived signed link into the admin-only
dev-docs site (/devdoc). Opening it sets an HttpOnly cookie and
redirects to the ticket-free URL; the cookie authorizes the
docs for 12h. Admin-only: session token + is_admin or
is_superadmin on the users record.

get.description:
Every users record: {users:[{id, name, email, github_login,
gitea_login, is_admin, is_superadmin, disabled, created,
updated}], total}.
Requires a session AND one of: is_admin, is_superadmin
(userAdminGuard — PATs rejected; the YAML admin lists are
only a boot-time seed for those flags).

403.description: user management requires admin / PAT auth not accepted

patch.description:
Body is a JSON object with any of {"disabled": bool,
"is_admin": bool} — at least one key required. disabled needs
admin-or-above; is_admin needs the is_superadmin flag.
Self-protection: nobody may disable
themselves or change their own is_admin; admins cannot
disable superadmins. is_superadmin is not patchable here.

get.description:
Returns {login, is_admin, is_user_admin, is_superadmin}
for the signed-in session user. login is the github_login,
falling back to gitea_login when only that is stamped.
All three flags read the users-record role flags (the
auth.admin_logins / superadmin_logins YAML lists only
seed them at boot): is_admin and is_user_admin are true
when the record holds is_admin or is_superadmin; the
SPA uses them to decide which admin surfaces to render.
Non-admins get false flags rather than a 403.
Session-token auth only (PAT auth
refused, same as /api/pat).

The discussion plus the first (or cursor-continued) page
of replies, oldest first, keyset-paginated by reply_id.
The ETag response header carries the body revision integer
used for If-Match CAS edits.

patch.description:
Author-only edit (the caller must be the body's author —
admins do not edit other people's words). Requires
If-Match with the current revision integer; a stale value
is a 409, the new body increments the revision and the
old/new pair is appended to the revision history. Editing
never reopens the status.

post.description:
Flat reply inside the discussion. Same identity/idempotency/
body-budget contract as discussion creation.

patch.description:
Same author-only CAS contract as the discussion body edit,
applied to one reply of the discussion.

get.description:
Append-only trail of one discussion: body_revisions (the
discussion's and its replies' edits: target / target_id /
old_body / new_body / editor / created_at) and
status_events (from / to / reason / actor / created_at),
both oldest-first.

patch.description:
Sets the status machine (pending / confirmed / retracted;
reopen allowed). `reason` is mandatory and every change is
appended to the status-event trail with the acting account.
Allowed for the discussion's root author or a platform
admin (users-record is_admin / is_superadmin — a user PAT
of an admin works; this is NOT the session-only admin
console gate). System PATs and everyone else get 403.

post.description:
Parses each input line (DOI, arXiv id, or paper URL),
resolve-or-mints it into the registry and enqueues the
multi-paradigm acquisition ladder (arXiv direct → OA
APIs → publisher URL patterns → landing page → LLM
agent fallback). Every fetched body is validated (%PDF-
magic, trailer, size bounds, HTML-disguise classification)
before it is stored and the MinerU pipeline is triggered.
Track progress via GET /api/downloader/jobs or the paper
detail acquisition block. Requires papers:write.

get.description:
In-process snapshot of downloader jobs (active + recent
terminal): per-paper state/phase, the winning strategy,
the full attempt trace and healthz-style counters. The
SPA's Robust Downloader page polls this every 2s while
jobs are active. Requires papers:read.

PostgreSQL-persisted snapshot of outbound fleet tasks (most
recently updated first, capped at 500): id, worker_id, state
(queued/running/staged/done/failed), identifier and error.
Unlike /api/downloader/jobs this survives server restarts.
Answers 200 with {enabled: false, jobs: []} when the remote
fleet is disabled. Requires papers:read.

200.description: {enabled: bool, jobs: [{id, worker_id, state, identifier, error?, updated_at}]}

get.description:
Liveness plus parallel dependency probes (rawstore, postgres,
registry). HTTP status is always 200; read data.status for the
real verdict ("healthy" | "degraded").

Returns the signed-in user's profile:
{id, email, name, avatar, github_login, gitea_login,
github_bound, gitea_bound, is_admin, is_superadmin,
created}.
avatar is the PocketBase file name — build the URL via the
PocketBase files API. *_bound reports which OAuth2
identities are linked to the record (the dashboard's
account-binding panels).

200.description: {id, email, name, avatar, github_login, gitea_login, github_bound, gitea_bound, is_admin, is_superadmin, created}

get.description:
The caller's per-user third-party search API key inventory
(backend name, masked hint, updated_at — never the key
material). enabled=false means the server has no encryption
secret configured and the whole feature is off. Session-only
(same reasoning as /api/pat: a leaked PAT must not read the
owner's third-party keys).

put.description:
Upserts the caller's API key for one backend (AES-256-GCM
encrypted at rest; injected into multi/agentic search calls
on the caller's behalf). The backend must be a catalog
backend with a user-key slot. 503 when the server has no
encryption secret configured. Session-only.

400.description: unknown backend / no user-key slot / empty key

delete.description:
Removes the caller's stored key for one backend (opaque 404
when absent). Session-only.

get.description:
Returns {metric, today, limit, llm_tokens} for the
agentic-search surface: today's call count, the caller's
effective daily limit (per-user override > plan >
search.agentic.daily_limit) and the LLM tokens consumed
today. Same metering shape as the agentic response's usage
block.

post.description:
Session-only (PAT auth rejected). Marks the pending request
as approved so the next /token poll mints the PAT bound to
the approving user.

get.description:
Session-only (PAT auth rejected). Returns the PAT spec
(name, description, scopes, expires_in_days) tied to a
pending user_code so the /<lang>/device page can show the
user what they're about to approve.

parameters.description: short user code (with or without dashes)
parameters.name: user_code

post.description:
RFC 8628 §3.1. Anonymous (no auth) — the CLI uses this to
obtain a device_code (kept secret, polled on /token) and a
short user_code that the human enters on the SPA's
/<lang>/device page after authenticating.

parameters.description: PAT spec to mint after approval
parameters.name: body

post.description:
Session-only (PAT auth rejected). Marks the pending request
as denied so the next /token poll returns "access_denied".

RFC 8628 §3.4 + §3.5. Anonymous. The CLI polls this with
device_code at the published interval until the server
returns the minted PAT plaintext (success) or an error
string ("authorization_pending", "slow_down", "expired_token",
"access_denied", "invalid_grant"). HTTP status is always
400 on errors per the RFC so the CLI can switch on `error`.
post.summary: Poll for PAT after device approval

get.description:
Paginated list of registry papers (merged tombstones
excluded). has_md filters on converted markdown present on
the paper's default asset (the "converted papers" page);
status filters by lifecycle; q is a case-insensitive title
substring; arxiv_id / doi / paper_id are exact-identity
filters (arxiv_id may carry a version suffix and doi a
URL prefix — both are canonicalized before matching).
Sorted by created_at (default) or updated_at,
descending. Requires the papers:read scope.

parameters.description: true = only papers with converted markdown on the default asset
parameters.name: has_md

parameters.description: exact arXiv id filter (version suffix optional)
parameters.name: arxiv_id

get.description:
Resolves comma-separated namespaced `kind:id` refs
(arxiv:… / openalex:… / doi:…) against the local OpenAlex
corpus. Returns per-ref {ref,title,authors,year,hosted,
has_md,resolved} plus corpus_available — hosted reports
whether QuantumAtlas hosts the ref, and has_md (meaningful
only when hosted) whether its default asset carries
converted markdown, so batch consumers learn both facts in
one call (≤200 refs per batch). Exact-by-id only; fuzzy
search is a separate deferred capability.

post.description:
Decides whether papers (qatlas-id / DOI / arXiv id /
OpenAlex id / paper URL / title) are already inside the
qatlas registry and returns the unified qa_… id.
Precision-first: identifiers match exactly after strict
normalization (trim / lowercase / known URL prefix /
arXiv vN); titles match only when EVERY word matches
(case-insensitive, order-insensitive). Merged papers
resolve to the surviving paper. Free-form `inputs` are
auto-detected per entry; the typed fields force a kind;
author/year narrow ambiguous title matches.
Upstream failures are never reported as empty matches: HTTP 504
denotes timeout; HTTP 502 includes a stable code distinguishing
transport, upstream HTTP and invalid response failures. Only the
numeric upstream_status is exposed, never private upstream bodies.
post.summary: Match paper identities against the registry

parameters.description: {inputs: [string], doi?, arxiv_id?, openalex_id?, qatlas_id?, url?, title?, author?, year?}
parameters.name: request

200.description: {results: [{input, kind, normalized, matched, qatlas_id, method, ambiguous, paper, candidates, truncated, reason}]}

post.description: Requires papers:write, registry/object storage and pdftotext. Accepts only public HTTPS URLs; every redirect and DNS destination is validated and pinned. The PDF title must match first-page front matter. No DOI is synthesized and distinct URLs are not title-merged. IACR ePrint landing/PDF forms share one eprint identity. Same work and SHA reuse an immutable source; changed bytes create a new source. No parse or Markdown is fabricated. HTTP Idempotency-Key response replay is not promised: check server state after a transport failure. At most two registrations acquire PDFs concurrently in one process; excess requests receive 503 with Retry-After before acquisition.

parameters.description: source_url HTTPS original, title (max 2000 UTF-8 bytes), authors (1..100, max 500 bytes each), year (1..9999)
parameters.name: request

400.description: invalid JSON, bibliographic fields or URL

get.description:
Counts of PDFs, markdown, JSON and mineru-pending papers from
the S3 paper index. Returns {available:false} when no S3
backend is configured.

Folds the .../markdown/status agent-decision surface into
one request: for each comma-separated id (qa_ surrogate,
arXiv id, or DOI — de-duplicated, max 200) the entry
carries requested_id, the resolved serving id (bare
arXiv inputs pin to the highest ingested asset version),
md_ready / pdf_ready store probes, the converter
state machine's state/phase labels, the default asset's
image_count, and an error field ("not found" for ids the
registry does not host; "catalog unavailable" when
PostgreSQL is down — per-entry, never failing the batch).

parameters.description: comma-separated paper ids (qa_... | arXiv id | DOI; max 200)
parameters.name: ids

200.description: {results:[{requested_id, resolved_id, md_ready, pdf_ready, image_count, phase, state, error}]}

post.description: Same claim_id/exact-source locator contract as /api/v1/papers/{id}/mineru-lease. Gate on: authenticated same-origin pdf_url with source_id,pdf_requires_auth:true,verifiedSHA; gate off: external arXiv URL+catalogSHA only. No NAS/S3 presigns or user authentication forwarding to providers.

201.description: claim granted (body is the claim record)

404.description: not claimable (no PDF in catalog, or markdown already exists)

409.description: already claimed by someone else (body includes existing claim details)
claim_id does not match the active claim

post.description:
Requires a COMPLETE supported docvortex.middle/schema_version 2.0 Middle (middle_json.json or supported layout.json) AND markdown.md/full.md; MD-only, ContentList-only, incomplete or invalid schema packages are 422. All valid producer-original relative paths/names/bytes, including every JSON and unknown file, are retained; originals are never renamed or reserialized. Traversal, absolute/backslash paths, duplicate names, symlinks, CRC/ZIP errors fail the whole archive. Limits: ZIP/member 128MiB, expanded aggregate 256MiB, at most 10000 files.
Writes create-only revision-scoped files into the new content bucket, verifies frozen exact PDF and every persisted member, writes separate manifest LAST, then publishes through PG (required). Every reupload is a new immutable revision/current publication; overwrite never changes historical revisions. Raw ZIP retention is optional; verified members+manifest are mandatory. No deferred-success indexing.

The {arxiv_id} slot also accepts a DOI for a published edition's exact already-uploaded PDF. Both paths share source-bound immutable bundle publication; there is no title/authors metadata override. PDF contribution establishes DOI metadata (see upload-pdf). A tier label records producer/request metadata, not proof of an executed provider quality mode.

post.description:
Freeze exact PDF bytes into the new content bucket and publish the alias/source identity through PostgreSQL (PG required, no deferred-success indexing). 200 for the same bound alias/SHA, 201 for a new frozen binding. The identifier alias is permanently bound to the first successful exact PDF: different bytes return 409 EVEN with overwrite=true. Same paper/SHA may reuse a source ID; semantic arXiv vN is not S3VersionId. Never mutate an old source or parse revision.

The {arxiv_id} slot also accepts a DOI (`10.<registrant>/<suffix>`)
for contributing a *published* version that may have no arXiv
preprint. DOI PDF bytes also use immutable content/{paper}/{source}/source.pdf;
its canonical import alias is separate from arXiv vN. The server resolves the DOI's title / authors /
linked arxiv id from OpenAlex — the contributor cannot supply
that metadata. The result is reported in `X-QAtlas-Verification`
and the JSON `verification` block; `verify=strict` rejects a
doi-not-found with 409 (or metadata-unavailable / unconfigured
with 503).

get.description:
Requires paper_access.enabled and papers:read for every ID, including qa_ aliases and Range. Disabled returns 404, not 410. Direct access does not require source-list rows first: a legacy PDF may be lazily frozen; no old MD/JSON/images are copied. Stored PDF retrieval requires no MinerU token or parsing. Frozen missing/corrupt bytes fail closed, never fall back to legacy/current/latest bytes.
source_id and version are mutually exclusive exact pins. arXiv vN is semantic source origin, not S3VersionId. Same paper/SHA may reuse a source ID. Explicit pin mismatch or ambiguity never substitutes a source/version. Full response SHA headers describe the whole PDF, not a partial Range.

get.description:
Requires paper_access.enabled and papers:read. This is derived Markdown-reading JSON, NOT raw Middle or Structured Content. Returns paper_id/source_id/revision/source_sha256/artifact_sha256/bundle_sha256?/renderer/format/content, request_scope, content_ranges, truncated, next_request and warnings?. page and block are 1-based exact producer indexes (not array offsets); block requires page. limit is a Unicode content budget, default 30000, max 100000.
An opaque cursor pins canonical paper/source/revision, PDF/Middle/bundle hashes, renderer and selection. Cursor-only resolves pins BEFORE selecting current; conflicting explicit pins/selectors are 409. Pinned failures never trigger repair, reparse, fallback or a current/latest substitution. Only content GET without a fixed revision/cursor may parse the selected verified source. source_id pins PDF, not a parse revision; absent PDF acquisition requires no source/revision/cursor pin. Old MD/JSON/images are ignored; legacy PDFs may be lazily frozen without deleting old storage.
Pending work returns 202 + Operation-Location=/api/papers/{canonical}/read/status?source_id=S once the source is known (otherwise retains the exact requested DOI/arXiv identity), plus Retry-After. Poll status without starting another job; only verified complete bundle readiness, not process Done or historical Middle existence, permits re-GET with fixed source/revision.

asset rows. The id is the surrogate paper_id ("qa_" +

get.description:
Issue-style discussion list for one paper, filtered by
anchor (parse_revision / page_idx / block_index), content
scope, type and status. Ordering is newest-first; the
cursor is the last discussion_id of the page (keyset).
scope=lean returns public+lean (the Lean view includes
shared public discussion); status=none selects statusless
notes. per_page defaults to 20, max 100. Requires
papers:read or comments:read; system PATs may read.

post.description:
Creates a root discussion anchored at (parse_revision,
page_idx, block_index) of the paper. actor and timestamps
are recorded server-side; the optional `model` string is a
pure client declaration. status may be set at creation
(then `reason` is required) or omitted for a statusless
note. Bodies are capped at comments.max_body_chars (default
20000 Unicode chars, 413 beyond, never truncated); requests
are capped at 1 MiB. Anchor misses 404 — never a
nearest-block fallback. Idempotency-Key: same key + same
request replays the original result; different request
409s. Requires a user identity (session or user PAT) with
comments:write — system PATs are read-only and get 403.

get.description:
Parse revisions of a paper: each row is one immutable
parse artifact (schema + schema_version + artifact
sha256) bound to the source it was parsed from. A
re-parse inserts a new revision and flips the
is_current pointer (current_revision_id); old artifacts
keep serving unchanged bytes. Requires login or
papers:read.

get.description:
Top-level blocks of one immutable parse revision, in
stable (page_idx, block index) order. Block indexes are
the parse's own public 1-based numbers and may be
non-contiguous (1,2,5,...); gaps are real — never
renumbered. page_idx is the original 0-based page index
(page_no in each item is the public 1-based number).
cursor is the opaque next_cursor token (keyset on the
last emitted block); per_page defaults to 20, max 100.
Requires paper_access.enabled plus login/papers:read, including historical revisions and qa_ identities; disabled is 404.

get.description:
Combined read of ONE block: source (paper + source PDF
identity + parse revision identity) + anchor (the
permanent comment anchor: canonical qa_, source_id,
parse_revision, schema, page_idx, block_index) +
content (the block's parsed value, original JSON under
raw) + discussions. Block lookup is EXACT on
(page_idx, block index): a non-contiguous index gap or a
page the parse lacks answers 404 — never a
nearest-block fallback. The same visual text under two
parses of one PDF is TWO distinct anchors; comments
never migrate between revisions. Original block content requires
paper_access.enabled plus login/papers:read for all IDs; comment
metadata does not provide an original-content gate bypass.

get.description:
A PNG crop of the ORIGINAL source PDF page rendered and
clipped to the block's [0,1]-normalized bbox — a real
page region, never a redraw of the parsed text. Honest
failures, never a fabricated image: the block carries
no bbox → 404 reason=no_bbox; the source PDF bytes are
missing → 404 reason=source_missing; the page is beyond
the source PDF → 404 reason=page_out_of_range; no PDF
rasterizer installed on the server → 503
reason=renderer_unavailable (operators install
poppler-utils or set paper_access.block_image_command;
resolution via paper_access.block_image_dpi, default
150). ETag is deterministic over (source sha, page,
bbox, dpi). Requires paper_access.enabled plus login/papers:read, including historical sources; Range/aliases do not bypass the gate.

Source PDF assets of a paper for the block-comments

post.description:
Same relay contract as /api/rag/retrieve but targeting
qatlas-rag's POST /v1/evidence: body forwarded verbatim,
reply streamed back as-is, 64 KiB cap, upstream errors
forwarded with their own status. Requires the papers:read
scope.

Forwards the request body verbatim to qatlas-rag's
POST /v1/retrieve (the retrieve request/response schema
belongs to the qatlas-rag repository — qatlasd only
authenticates the caller and relays, so schema changes
never need a qatlasd release) and streams the reply back
as-is. Bodies are capped at 64 KiB. rag.remote disabled →
503 "rag service not configured"; microservice
unreachable → 503 "rag unreachable: …"; a non-2xx
upstream reply is forwarded with its own status + body so
clients see the rag error schema. Requires the
papers:read scope.

Fans one search entry out to the configured providers
(catalog / arxiv / openalex / remote), merges hits by paper
identity (DOI > arXiv > title hash) and resolve-or-mints each
identity-anchored hit against the paper registry. Newly minted
papers carry created=true as metadata only: search does not
download papers or submit conversion tasks. Select identifiers
explicitly via POST /api/downloader/fetch. Title-only hits return as un-minted
candidates. The entry may carry an identity (arxiv_id / doi)
instead of free text — identity fields are forwarded to the
remote provider for identity-aware lookups; an entry with
none of text / title / arxiv_id / doi is a 400. Each minted
result also carries its hosting summary: has_md / has_pdf /
status from the registry default asset (omitted when the
registry is unavailable). Requires the papers:read scope.

parameters.name: body

post.description:
One multi-source search through the agentic backend
(remote qatlas-search microservice or the local runner),
optionally with an LLM conclusion ({"agent": false} skips
it). The body is a search entry plus "agent" and "sources"
extensions; identity fields (arxiv_id / doi / title) are
forwarded so identity-only entries run identity lookups
instead of an empty query — an entry with none of text /
title / arxiv_id / doi is a 400 (before metering). Every
call is metered per user per day (usage block); a failed
upstream is refunded. Results mirror POST /api/search,
including the has_md / has_pdf / status hosting summary
on minted results. Anchoring is metadata-only; downloads require
explicit POST /api/downloader/fetch. Requires the papers:read scope plus a
user-bound credential (system PATs get 403).

post.description:
Proxies one mode="multi" call to the qatlas-search
microservice: every requested backend returns its own raw
hit list (the source's own order), with NO cross-backend
merge or ranking. The caller's stored third-party API keys
(configured in the dashboard) are decrypted and forwarded so
key-requiring backends run under the user's credentials.
Provide text or doi (at least one nonblank). A DOI-only request
forwards doi with an empty query for identity-aware lookup;
nonempty text retains text-search semantics when both are supplied.
Identity-anchored hits (DOI / arXiv id) are resolve-or-
minted as metadata only before the response, without downloads
or conversion tasks, and carry the server-side
enrichment paper_id / created / has_md / status (the
hosting summary is omitted when the registry is
unavailable). Title-only hits — no DOI, no arXiv id — are
never minted and carry none of these fields.
Requires the papers:read scope; 503 when search.remote is
disabled; 502 when the microservice call fails.

Search anchors metadata only; downloading selected identifiers requires POST /api/downloader/fetch.
Remote-only fused search with ranking=scorer and agent=false. Requires papers:read. Recompiles the supplied program on every request. No LLM calls. Preserves one globally ordered hit list including title-only candidates and custom score explanations; only returned identity-anchored hits are resolve-or-minted. Scores are neither normalized nor probabilities.

One successful generation consumes one shared Agentic daily unit; failures refund the unit while recording known token usage. At most one internal repair.

post.description:
Results are anchored as metadata only, without downloads or conversion tasks; selected identifiers require POST /api/downloader/fetch.
Keywords, author/year/venue/citation rules and agentic planning are owned by qatlas-search. Rules filter a bounded retrieved set, not an exhaustive corpus. Per-user backend keys are injected by qatlasd and cannot be supplied by callers.

get.description:
Capability discovery: mode / version / engine plus a
capabilities block — paper_access, markdown_delivery,
pdf_delivery (available when paper_access is enabled;
stored PDF delivery requires no MinerU token), agentic_search, and a nested mineru
object (enabled / on_demand). Privacy mirrors /api/health:
anonymous callers see the booleans only; authenticated
callers (system PAT or session) additionally get
mineru.daily_cap and mineru.converted_today from the
batch-scheduler snapshot. Note the quota semantics:
daily_cap bounds explicit operator/manual batch runs;
there is no automatic nightly, boot, PDF-ingest or bulk
conversion. Only explicit content access triggers lazy
source-bound inference; stored PDF reads are token-independent.
Manual and on-demand work still share upstream token quotas.

post.description: Acquires the same MinerU processing lease returned by the claim path. The response body uses claim_id as the lease identifier. With paper_access enabled, pdf_url is a same-origin authenticated exact-source locator, source_id/pdf_requires_auth:true and verified PDF SHA are returned; never forward the user's auth to an external parser. Download exact bytes with auth, then use provider upload. With the gate off, only the external arXiv URL and grant catalog SHA are returned; no hosted PDF bytes.

201.description: lease granted (body is the lease record; claim_id identifies the lease)

404.description: not claimable (no PDF in catalog, or markdown already exists)

409.description: already leased by someone else (body includes existing lease details)

delete.description: Releases a MinerU processing lease by claim_id.

409.description: claim_id does not match the active lease

BearerAuth.description:
"Bearer <token>" — two credential shapes
accepted: a Personal Access Token
(`Authorization: Bearer qat_...`, minted at
`/pat` after GitHub OAuth login), or the
config-loaded system PAT (set
`system_pat.token` in config.yaml on the
server, send the plaintext as
`Authorization: Bearer <value>`).
Browser callers are authenticated through
pb.authStore (no copy step) — only non-browser
callers need an explicit bearer.
